title: Fppf presentation of an affine action quotient without smoothness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $H$ an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $E$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra with a rational $H$-action. Here rational means a $k$-algebra coaction $\rho_E:E\to E\otimes_k k[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, and $E^H=\{e:\rho_E(e)=e\otimes1\}$. For definiteness, use left actions: if $b:U\times_kH\to U$ is dual to $\rho_E$, put $h\cdot u=b(u,h^{-1})$; use left translation for torsors. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^H)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define $\mathcal X=[U/H]$ as the stack on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] whose objects over $T$ are pairs $(P,f)$, with $P\to T$ an $H_T$-torsor and $f:P\to U$ equivariant; arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with $f$. A torsor means a scheme with an $H_T$-action that becomes the translation action on $H_T$ after an fppf covering of $T$. Then $\mathcal X$ is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic stack with affine diagonal, with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] (algebraic stack has the meaning in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]). The trivial torsor defines $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$, which is representable, faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] after scheme charts. For every algebraic-stack base change of $\pi$, the induced map of underlying spaces is open and surjective. The invariant map $U\to Y$ descends to a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ with $\phi\pi$ induced by $E^H\hookrightarrow E$. The underlying space of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the quotient topology from a smooth surjective scheme atlas. No smoothness of $H$ or finite generation of $E^H$ is required.

source.place: Tags 06FI (theorem-flat-groupoid-gives-algebraic-stack), 06FH (lemma-flat-quotient-flat-presentation); spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 04M9 (lemma-quotient-stack-2-cartesian); stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06R7 (lemma-fppf-open). Apply to the affine action groupoid.

proof.text: Put $C=k[H]$. Its underlying $k$-module is flat by the field-module lemma; the affine flatness criterion makes $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ flat. Every ideal in a field is either zero or the whole field, so $k$ is Noetherian; since $C$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra it is finitely presented. The affine definition of local finite presentation therefore applies to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Write $b:U\times_kH\to U$ for the right action dual to $\rho_E$, and use the left action $a(h,u)=b(u,h^{-1})$. Equivalently $a^*=(S\otimes1)\tau\rho_E$, with $S$ pullback by group inversion and $\tau$ the tensor-factor swap. Then the tensor-product description of affine fibre products and the bijection between maps into an affine scheme and ring maps turn its two identities into the right-action identities; inversion converts them into the left-action identities. Form $R=H\times_kU$ with $s(h,u)=u$, $t(h,u)=hu$, identity $(1,u)$, inverse $(h,u)\mapsto(h^{-1},hu)$ and composition $(h,gu)\circ(g,u)=(hg,u)$. The group and action identities give the groupoid identities on every test scheme. The map $s$ is a base change of $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; $t=s\circ i$ with $i$ the displayed involution. Thus both maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by base-change and composition calculus.

source.place: Tags 06FI, 06FH, hypotheses; algebra.tex Tag 00FP; affine action-groupoid specialization

proof.text: Apply the flat-groupoid theorem to $(U,R,s,t)$ to obtain an algebraic stack $\mathcal Q$, a representable flat locally finitely presented surjection $p:U\to\mathcal Q$, and $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$. The affine-group torsor comparison, which imposes no smoothness assumption, identifies $\mathcal Q$ with the $\mathcal X$ in the statement and $p$ with its trivial-torsor map $\pi$. In particular the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Surjectivity together with flatness is the stated faithful flatness. For the chart calculus used here and below, schemes are algebraic stacks with identity atlas: their fppf sheaf axiom follows from fpqc descent of morphisms and the fact that an fppf cover is fpqc; their diagonal is represented by ordinary scheme fibre products. No smoothness of $\pi$ is asserted.

Consider $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ after the cover $q:U\times_kU\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$. Products here are algebraic stacks by the fibre-product lemma. Factor $q$ as two base changes of $\pi$; the chart calculus shows that $q$ is representable, flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. By $U\times_{\mathcal X}U\simeq R$, the pullback of the diagonal is $(t,s):R\to U\times_kU$ (up to the harmless interchange of the two factors). Both schemes are affine by the tensor-product description. A morphism between affine schemes is affine: it is the map of spectra induced by its coordinate-ring map. The fppf-locality theorem for representable stack morphisms, with property affine, now gives an affine diagonal of $\mathcal X/k$. This also gives an affine absolute diagonal: for any two maps to $\mathcal X$ over a test scheme, the structural maps to $k$ must agree to have an isomorphism; their equalizer is a closed subscheme because the multiplication map $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k\to k$ is surjective. On this affine closed equalizer the relative Isom-space is affine. On every affine test scheme an affine diagonal is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated, by affine-morphism permanence. Thus $\mathcal X$ is quasi-separated in the stated stack convention.

source.place: Tag 04M9; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XD; affine diagonal calculation

proof.text: Let $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$ be any algebraic-stack base change and put $\mathcal W=U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$. The fibre-product lemma makes $\mathcal W$ algebraic. Base-change calculus makes $\mathcal W\to\mathcal Z$ flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Z$. The base change $W=U\times_{\mathcal X}V\to V$ is a map of algebraic spaces flat and locally of finite presentation, so its map on point spaces is open by the space openness lemma. For any open subset $O\subseteq|\mathcal W|$, its inverse image in $|W|$ is open: $W\to\mathcal W$ is a smooth surjection, and the atlas quotient topology (or an etale scheme atlas of $W$) gives continuity. The image of that inverse image in $|V|$ is exactly the preimage of the image of $O$ in $|\mathcal Z|$. This equality follows by forming the fibre product of field-valued objects after a common field extension, including its required isomorphism. It is open by openness of $W\to V$. The quotient topology of the smooth atlas $V\to\mathcal Z$ shows that the image of $O$ is open. Surjectivity is already preserved by base change, proving the assertion for every $\mathcal Z$.

source.place: Tag 06R7 (lemma-fppf-open), its atlas proof, after arbitrary base change

proof.text: The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-compact. Apply the quasi-compact-surjection criterion to the surjection $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$ from step 2. It follows that $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact; combined with step 3 this proves all asserted finiteness properties of $\mathcal X$. This use requires only surjectivity of $\pi$, not that $\pi$ be a smooth atlas.

Let $r:U\to Y$ correspond to $E^H\hookrightarrow E$. For $e\in E^H$, the two maps from $E^H$ to $E\otimes_k C$ induced by $r\circ a$ and $r\circ\operatorname{pr}_U$ send $e$ to the same invariant tensor (in $C\otimes_kE$, it is $1\otimes e$, since applying the antipode to $1$ preserves $1$). The affine Hom bijection gives equality of these two morphisms. For an object $(P,f)$ over $T$, choose an fppf trivialization of $P$ with corresponding local maps $x_i:T_i\to U$. The transition arrows act by elements of $H$, so the maps $r x_i$ agree on overlaps. Fppf covers are fpqc, and fpqc descent of morphisms to the scheme $Y$ gives a unique $T\to Y$. Uniqueness shows compatibility with pullback and with equivariant isomorphisms, so these maps define $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$. On a trivial torsor this gives $r$ itself, proving $\phi\pi=r$. This explicit construction uses no finite generation of $E^H$.

source.place: Tag 04WM, explicit torsor description; descent.tex Tag 023Q; invariant equalizer calculation

proof.text: The scheme $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^H)$ is affine, even when $E^H$ is not finitely generated. It is quasi-separated by affine-scheme qcqs. This agrees with the stack convention: a scheme diagonal is a monomorphism, hence its own relative diagonal is an isomorphism, so the additional quasi-separatedness condition on that representable diagonal is automatic. By steps 3 and 5, $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply algebraic-stack qcqs permanence to $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$. Its hypotheses concern precisely these source and target properties and impose no representability or Noetherian condition. The resulting quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $\phi$ complete the proof.
